title: Fake IT MFA Push
scenario: IT says to approve MFA prompts so they can fix your account.

answers.A: Act immediately because the request sounds urgent and important.
answers.B: Use the approved company system or verified process.
answers.C: Escalate to IT, finance, HR, legal, or your manager through official channels.
answers.D: Reply to the sender asking them to confirm the request.

explanation: Fake IT MFA Push: the trap is to get access to an account, code, password, or permission. The safer move is to verify through an official or approved channel, not to act before verifying.
proTip: Never approve MFA prompts you did not initiate.
